papers.title: Modifications of Dental Implant Surfaces at the Micro- and Nano-Level for Enhanced Osseointegration.
papers.abstract: This review paper describes several recent modification methods for biocompatible titanium dental implant surfaces. The micro-roughened surfaces reviewed in the literature are sandblasted, large-grit, acid-etched, and anodically oxidized. These globally-used surfaces have been clinically investigated, showing survival rates higher than 95%. In the past, dental clinicians believed that eukaryotic cells for osteogenesis did not recognize the changes of the nanostructures of dental implant surfaces. However, research findings have recently shown that osteogenic cells respond to chemical and morphological changes at a nanoscale on the surfaces, including titanium dioxide nanotube arrangements, functional peptide coatings, fluoride treatments, calcium-phosphorus applications, and ultraviolet photofunctionalization. Some of the nano-level modifications have not yet been clinically evaluated. However, these modified dental implant surfaces at the nanoscale have shown excellent in vitro and in vivo results, and thus promising potential future clinical use.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文综述了牙科植入物表面的微纳米级改性方法，但未涉及激光粉末床熔融增材制造技术。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a review of dental implant surface modifications without any LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing, fatigue analysis, or stress shielding consideration.

summary_zh.motivation: 综述钛种植体表面微纳改性方法以促进骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 总结了喷砂、酸蚀、阳极氧化、纳米管、肽涂层等改性技术。
summary_zh.result: 微米级表面临床存活率>95%，纳米级改性体外/体内结果优异。
summary_zh.validation: 引用临床研究和体外/体内实验数据。

summary_en.motivation: This review aims to summarize recent surface modification methods for titanium dental implants that enhance osseointegration.
summary_en.method: It covers micro-roughened surfaces (sandblasted, acid-etched, anodized) and nano-level modifications (TiO2 nanotubes, peptide coatings, fluoride, CaP, UV photofunctionalization).
summary_en.result: Micro-roughened surfaces achieve >95% clinical survival, while nano-modifications show promising in vitro and in vivo outcomes.
summary_en.validation: Validation is drawn from clinical studies for micro-topographies and from preclinical studies for nano-modifications.
